Keep these files concise. Put implementation-specific guidance in the nearest module-level `AGENTS.md` or README. ## Project Structure - App code: `src/app/**` - Server runtime and APIs: `src/server/**` - Data layer: `src/db/**` - Shared contracts/types/utilities: `src/shared/**` and `src/types/**` - Unit tests: `*.spec.ts` in `src/**` - Playwright tests: `tests/**` - Legacy e2e reference: `e2e/**` - Assets/public: `public/` - Theming: `src/styles.scss` and `_theme-colors.scss` Start with the nearest applicable module guidance: - `src/app/AGENTS.md` - `src/server/AGENTS.md` - `src/db/AGENTS.md` - `tests/AGENTS.md` More specific guidance may exist deeper in some subtrees. ## Build, Test, and Development Commands - `bun run dev:start` - refresh worktree-local runtime env and run Angular dev server at the generated `BASE_URL`. - `bun run build:app` - build client + server bundles. - `bun run test:unit` - run unit tests. - `bun run test:unit:server` - run server unit tests. - `bun run test:e2e` - run Playwright e2e. - `bun run test:e2e:integration` - run credential-gated Playwright integration projects. - `bun run test:e2e:docs` - run Playwright documentation tests. - `bun run test:e2e:install` - install the local Playwright browser binaries. - `bun run lint` - lint with autofix. - …

> AGENT

I checked the CI path. The bandwidth risk is not from a Font Awesome kit in the app; the repo uses public npm packages: - `@fortawesome/angular-fontawesome` - `@fortawesome/free-brands-svg-icons` - `@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons` The likely cause was repeated CI dependency installs. Locally, this has already been addressed in commit `ed2675278`: - E2E now warms Bun package cache, `node_modules`, Playwright browser cache, and Docker build cache once. - Matrix E2E jobs restore `node_modules` and refuse to run another `bun install` if the warm cache did not restore, avoiding three parallel Font Awesome package downloads. - Docker Compose CI builds use `.github/docker-compose.build-cache.yml`, with BuildKit/GHA/local cache enabled, so Dockerfile `bun install` layers are reused. - CI forces `@fortawesome` to `https://registry.npmjs.org/` and rejects repo `.npmrc`, avoiding accidental Font Awesome private/pro registry usage. - Copilot setup also restores the same caches and refuses a registry install on cache miss. So yes, caching is the right fix, and it’s already in the local PR branch. The remaining problem is that I still cannot push it: SSH signing fails locally, and HTTPS push is blocked because the current GitHub token lacks `workflow` scope for `.github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml`.

Current remote PR workflow still: - runs the E2E matrix in parallel - runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in each matrix job - clears Bun cache on retry with `bun pm cache rm` - has only a simple Bun cache keyed by `bun.lock` Local branch already changes that to: - serial `warm-ci-caches` job - shared `~/.bun/install/cache` - cached `node_modules` - matrix jobs install offline or fail instead of re-downloading - public `@fortawesome` registry override - guards against `.npmrc`, `FONT_AWESOME_TOKEN`, `npm.fontawesome.com`, and pro/duotone/sharp FontAwesome packages - Docker BuildKit cache with locked Bun cache mounts - Copilot setup uses the same cache/offline policy So yes, caching is the right fix, and it is already in the local commits. The urgent next step is getting this branch pushed with a GitHub token that has `workflow` scope; until then GitHub keeps running the old bandwidth-heavy workflow.
